current.text: Wagler is a rookie. The Clippers took him with the number five overall pick.
He is projected as the backup point guard behind Darius Garland, ninth in the Clippers' bench order. He plays the same position as Garland.
Experts do not expect him to start or play 30 minutes. One expects about 25 minutes. Garland, Beal, Dunn, Sanders and Strus all compete for guard minutes.

Experts say a market ADP around 117 to 124 is far too high. He is more likely to finish outside the top 250 than inside the top 100, and he should not be drafted in standard formats. At most he is a stash around pick 170 in 16-team leagues.
The Clippers' roster is not set up to hand the offense to rookies.
The Clippers are expected to run a trial season with long rotations and many players tested. Coach Ty Lue often changes his rotation choices.
The Clippers play 4-3-4 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, which end March 28. They have 13 back-to-backs, one of the lowest totals in the league.
He played better defense than expected at Summer League.

durable.text: He is a skilled, high-IQ guard. He can pull up off screens and catch and shoot.
He has limited athleticism. He did not dunk once at Illinois.
The newest expert expects him to shoot very poorly and to have efficiency problems.
His play swings a lot. He looked terrible at times but had some high-level scoring games.

note: Yahoo ranks him 210 and ESPN 208, with values of 0 USD on both and no auction history in our league. The experts agree he should not be drafted in a 12-team league where 144 players go, even if other markets take him around ADP 117. Leave him on waivers and watch his minutes behind Garland early in the season, mainly while Beal is out. His projections show no clear category edge (4.0 assists, 45.9% FG), so only a clearly bigger role would make him worth a pickup.
